Order:

1. Revisionists Rajdeep Singh Pahwa, Devinder Kaur Pahwa and Divyajot Kaur have filed the present revision petition challenging the impugned order dated 02.05.2024 whereby Ld.
MM(Mahila Court)-03 West had framed charges u/s 498A/34 against all of them and u/s 406/34 IPC against accused Devinder Kaur Pahwa and Divyajot Kaur.

Perusal of impugned order shows that in addition to the three revisionist, who are accused no.2, 3 and 4 before Ld. Trial Court, accused no.1 Ramandeep Singh was also charged for offence u/s 498A/34 IPC vide impugned order dated 02.05.2024.
However, he has not challenged the impugned order.
Similarly accused no.1 Ramandeep Singh and accused no.2 Rajdeep Singh Pahwa were discharged from offence u/s 406/34 IPC
but the said discharge has not been challenged either by the State or by complainant.
It is submitted that there is no other revision petition filed against the impugned order dated 02.05.2024 by any of the parties pending in any other court.

2. Revisionists Rajdeep Singh Pahwa, Devinder Kaur Pahwa and Divyajot Kaur are the accused no.
2, 3 and 4 before Ld. Trial Court.
Accused no.1 Ramandeep Singh is not party to the present revision petition.
Complainant has been impleaded as respondent no.2 in the present petition while Respondent no. 1 is the State.
For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred to by their nomenclature before Ld. Trial Court.
3. Arguments on the revision petition heard.
Record carefully perused.

BRIEF FACTS:
4. Brief facts of the case necessary for disposal of the present revision petition are that the present FIR was registered on 21.09.2022 on the basis of a complaint dated 25.06.2022 made by complainant Gulneet Kaur.
As per the allegations in the complaint, marriage of the complainant was solemnized with accused no.1 Ramandeep Singh on 24.02.2019.
Accused no.2 is the father-in-law of the complainant, accused no.3 is her mother- in-law and accused no.4 is her sister-in-law.

5. It is alleged in the complaint that at the time of marriage, parents of the complainant had fulfilled all the dowry demands raised by her husband and parents-in-law and spent huge amount beyond their financial ability by taking loans.
The marriage was solemnized at Surya Grand, Rajouri Garden and after marriage, she went to her matrimonial house at CR Park.
Her mother-in- law/A-3 immediately took all her jewelery articles from her on the pretext that she will keep the same in safe custody and promised to return the same as and when demanded.
When she informed about it to her husband/A-1, he got annoyed and pressurized her to do as directed by her mother-in-law.

She Rajdeep Singh Pahwa vs The State on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97967093/
2 handed over her jewelery articles to accused no.3, however thereafter, she was never allowed to use the same despite several demands.

sentences.text: 6. Her husband started quarreling with her and shouted upon her within 10 days of her marriage without any reason and her in- laws also supported him.
Her husband/A-1 also abused her and made forcible physical relations with her.
She was beaten by her husband and when she informed about his conduct to her mother- in-law/A-3, she asked her to keep mum and threatened her not to inform her parents.

She was also taunted for low-key wedding organized by her parents and low quality goods given in the wedding by her husband and parents-in-laws and when she objected, they shouted at her and abused her.
They also asked her to go to her parental home and asked for money for the things needed in her matrimonial house.
They asked her to get some capital from her parents for setting up business for her husband and also asked her to arrange money from her parents for going of her husband to Canada.
However, she refused as she knew the financial condition of her parents.
On her refusal, she was pressurized to demand 1/3 share in the property of her father.
When she refused for this also, they restricted her contact with her parents.
7. Her parents-in-law forcefully made her to resign from her job in August 2019 and she became completely financially dependent upon her husband.
Her mother-in-law also restricted her in speaking to the neighbours.
She was even abused and embarrassed in front of her family members in February 2020 during her cousin's wedding.

She was also forced to do all the household chores,
even during her ill health.

She was also blamed when firstly she and thereafter her father-in-law,
mother- in-law and sister-in-law got infected with Covid-19 virus.
Her father-in-law abused her on this issue and when she asked for support from her husband, he slapped her and pulled her hair.
After that incident, she was frequently beaten by her husband and abused without any reason.

8. In September 2020, she convinced her husband and in- laws to re-join her job on the condition that she shall hand over her entire salary to her husband, however her sister-in-law/A-4 was not happy with this and tried to instigate her husband saying that she was having male friends at her work place.
Her husband also slapped her on this issue without listening to her.
Her husband and in-laws forced her to ask her parents to finance the new flat that her in-laws were purchasing in Gurugram.
She refused and was abused and restrained to even speak to her parents.
Her parents were not even invited for house warming party for the new flat.

In July 2021, when her husband's Taya Ji expired, her parents visited their new house to offer condolence and at that time her in-laws asked them to finance the construction of modular kitchen which was under construction at that time.
Her parents had borne the entire expenses in this regard.
9. She was continuously harassed and made to work like a maid and also threatened for divorce.
Her sister-in-law/A-4 took all her party wear clothes and accessories, which were given by her parents on various occasions.
She was also not given proper food.
She was so disturbed that she had to visit the therapist due to which her husband and in-laws started calling her a mentally retarded person.

On 13.04.2022, her husband and in-laws asked for all the money lying in bank account, which she refused, on which her husband and father-in-law became annoyed and were about to beat her up Rajdeep Singh Pahwa vs The State on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97967093/
3 when she locked her up in a bed room and called her parents.

sentences.text: Her parents came and she was manhandled by her husband even in their presence and was thrown out of her matrimonial home.
10. After completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed by the IO against all the accused persons for offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC.
The accused persons were summoned.

11. Arguments on the point of charge were heard on behalf of the accused persons as well as the complainant and thereafter, vide impugned order dated 02.05.2024 charges were directed to be framed against the accused persons.
GROUNDS OF REVISION/ARGUMENTS OF REVISIONISTS/ACCUSED PERSONS:

12. In the present revision petition, the impugned order has been challenged on the ground that Ld.
Trial Court has ignored the fact that there are no specific allegations against A-2 to A-4 and they have been simply roped in the present FIR being the relatives of husband of the complainant.

Ld.
Trial Court has failed to appreciate the fact that the case of the prosecution lacks credibility as none of the allegations with respect to cruelty inflicted upon the complainant are supported by any MLC or any medical document.

The only prescription of a spiritual center namely "Grace and Gracious"
filed on record lacks credibility as it is not a medical prescription.
Ld. Trial Court had ignored the fact that there was a delay of more than two months in filing the complaint after the complainant left matrimonial home on 13.04.2022.
Moreover, there are various contradictions in the statements of the complainant herself regarding payments made by her parents towards construction of modular kitchen.
Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the charges framed against the petitioners were groundless and there was no shred of evidence against them on record.
Moreover, the allegations of dowry given in marriage were not supported by any proper bills.
Entire complaint is filed with false and fabricated allegations and is a sheer misuse and abuse of process of law.
Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that even if the entire material on record is taken at its face value, it does not make out any prima facie case against the revisionists.
The allegations are general without any specific date and time and are highly improbable, unbelievable and untrustworthy as they are neither supported by any complaint nor any medical document.

Ld. Trial Court has ignored the contradictions in the statements of the complainant recorded at various stages and has also failed to appreciate that the essential ingredients of offence u/s 406 IPC are not made out from the allegations contained in the complaint.
Moreover, during investigation entire belongings of the complainant have already been returned to her.
Thus, the impugned order is bad in law and deserves to be set-aside.
Counsel for the Revisionist has argued in line with the grounds of revision and has prayed for setting-aside the impugned order of charge qua the revisionists.

Reliance has been placed on the decision of various superior courts whereby courts have been directed to be careful in proceeding against distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths and it has been held that the relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

ARGUMENTS OF RESPONDENTS/STATE &
COMPLAINANT:
16.
Per contra, the present revision petition is vehemently opposed on behalf of the State as well as the complainant.
It is submitted that there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned order dated 02.05.2024.
It is a well reasoned order passed on the basis of material available on record.
It is not a stereotype order but shows clear application of mind by Ld. Trial Court as charge under all the sections has not been framed against all the accused persons.
Various allegations have been categorically considered and thereafter two of the accused persons have been discharged for offence u/s 406/34 IPC.
Mere contention of the revisionist that the allegations made in the complaint are not supported by any medical document or any previous complaint is not sufficient to discharge the accused persons.
It is a common practice that in matrimonial disputes efforts are generally made to compromise the matter and save the relationship before rushing to the police authorities at the first instance.
The complainant has clearly explained her intention of saving her relationship in her complaint by not reporting the matter even to her parents initially.
The allegations made in the complaint are specific giving the specific incidents and role of each and every accused person.
At this stage of consideration of charge only a prima facie has to be seen and the court cannot appreciate the detailed evidence which is yet to be produced.
It is submitted that there is no reason to interfere with the impugned order as there is no illegality and infirmity in the same.
Hence, dismissal of the present revision petition is prayed.
17. Ld. Counsel for the respondent no.2/complainant has relied upon following citations in support of his arguments.
(I) Wazirchand & Anrs Vs. State of Haryana, AIR 1989 SC 378, wherein the essential ingredients of Section 498A IPC have been discussed.

sentences.text: I have heard the submissions made on behalf of parties and carefully perused the record as well as the citations relied upon by them.

20. The scope of enquiry, a judge is required to make while considering the question of framing of charges has been considered by the Apex Court in Union of India Vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4.

entities.text: Union of India Vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After an exhaustive survey of the case law on the point, the Apex court has laid down the following principles:-
" (1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.

(2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained the Court will be, fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.
(3) The test to determine a prima facie case would be naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application.

By and large however, if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.

(4) That in exercising his jurisdiction under section 227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and experienced Judge cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouth-piece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.

This however,
does not mean that the Judge should make a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial."
21. Section 498A IPC provides punishment for cruelty to a woman by her husband or relative of her husband.
The term cruelty within the meaning of Section 498A IPC has been explained in the explanation to the said section.
It consists of two clauses (a) and (b).

To attract Section 498A IPC, it must be established that the cruelty or harassment to wife was to force her to cause grave bodily injury to herself or to commit suicide; or the harassment was to compel her to fulfill illegal demands of dowry.

Thus, every type of harassment or cruelty would not attract Section 498A IPC.
22.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are two essential ingredient for the offence of criminal breach of trust.

Firstly, the accused must be entrusted with property or dominion over it and secondly, he must have dishonestly misappropriated the property or converted it to his own use or disposed it off in voilation of any trust.

24. I have carefully perused the complaint on which present FIR has been registered as well as the documents annexed with the chargesheet and the statement of witnesses recorded u/s 161 CrPC.
25.

Considering the overall material available on record, no infirmity or illegality is found in the order dated 02.05.2024 directing framing of charge against all the accused persons for offences u/s 498A/34 IPC and against accused Devinder Kaur and Divyajot Kaur u/s 406/34 IPC as prima facie case for offences under those sections is reflected from the material available on record.
The revisionists had made almost identical submissions before Ld. Trial Court as the grounds of revision pleaded before this court.

The said submissions regarding absence of MLC, previous complaints and jewelery bills as well as return of dowry articles are duly reflected in impugned order dated 02.05.2024 and have been considered by Ld. Trial Court.

In the present case, no ground is made out for discharge of accused persons as there are specific allegations of demands of dowry as well as cruelty meted out to the complainant at the hands of the accused persons in the complaint as well as subsequent statements recorded during investigation.

Minor contradictions here and there cannot be a ground for discharging the accused persons as the credibility and the veracity of the statement of witnesses is yet to be tested after appreciation of evidence led by both the parties.

Moreover, as per record, although certain dowry articles have been returned by the accused persons to the complainant during investigation, however, they are the articles as per their own admitted list and not as per the list of istridhan articles filed by the complainant.

Thus, whether or not the Jewellery and other istridhan articles entrusted to accused no.3 and 4 (as per allegations) have been misappropriated by them is a disputed question of fact which can be appreciated only after appreciation of evidence led by both the parties.
26. As discussed above even a strong suspicion is sufficient to frame charges against the accused persons and meticulous examination of the evidence is not required at that stage.

Considering the reasons given above and the impugned order dated 02.05.2024, I am of the opinion that all the material available on record has been duly considered by Ld. Trial Court while directing of framing of charges.

This does not appear to be a case which should be closed at the stage of charge as at the stage of framing of charge only a prima facie view is required to be taken and it is not required to be considered if the evidence to be adduced is sufficient to base the conviction.
